Dedicated vs Hosted fallback and failover
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of Cloud - Orchid), Ethan (Network Eng), Lena (Security), Samir (CTO - joined later)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood, Carlos is our SE, we'll mostly do a private/VPC discovery today to understand your network constraints, region needs, and security requirements.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks, Maya. quick context from our side — Orchid runs a multi-region infra, primary workloads in us-west-2 and backups in eu-west-1. we have strict egress policies, everything must go through our proxy and we prefer private connectivity.
[00:34] Carlos: Got it. do you have an existing transit gateway or are you using VPC peering today between those regions?
[00:40] Ethan: We route via a transit gateway in AWS, yes. also we have a hub VPC that hosts our NAT/proxies, and we want Redwood to not have to traverse public internet for inference traffic.
[00:53] Lena: Security side — we need KMS integration for key ownership, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SSO via SAML, and RBAC for teams. also data residency for EU requests must stay in eu-west-1.
[01:08] Maya: Perfect, that's really helpful. so we support several private connectivity options: VPC peering (directly between Redwood Private VPC and customer VPC), AWS Transit Gateway attachments, and PrivateLink / interface endpoints. each has tradeoffs: peering is simple but doesn't scale across many accounts, TGW is excellent for centralized routing, and PrivateLink gives endpoint-level isolation and simpler DNS.
[01:34] Priya: we were leaning toward TGW to keep things consistent. with Peering we'd need multiple peerings per account which is a pain. what about cross-region — can Redwood host nodes in eu-west-1 and attach to our TGW there?
[01:49] Carlos: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed in specific regions; we can provision private VPCs in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. for TGW the standard pattern is to attach our Redwood VPC to your TGW via a TGW attachment; Redwood SEs coordinate the route propagation. latency wise, keeping inference in-region is best for EU residency and for reducing RTT.
[02:10] Ethan: ok, and DNS? if we use PrivateLink, we want our internal DNS to resolve the private endpoint cname to the interface endpoints. Any gotchas?
[02:19] Carlos: you can enable private DNS on the interface endpoint; Redwood exposes an internal hostname and the PrivateLink interface will register in your VPC. caveat — if you're doing split-horizon DNS or custom resolvers you might need to override some records. we also provide sample Resolver rules.
[02:34] Priya: do you require any specific ports or security group rules? our security team is strict.
[02:39] Carlos: primarily HTTPS (443) outbound from your app to the private endpoint. for internal control channels we may use a few management ports, but we try to keep the surface minimal and document them in the peering/TGW runbook. we'll provide exact SGs and NACLs in the checklist.
[02:54] Lena: about KMS, we need customer-managed keys. will Redwood use our key to encrypt model cache or tokens at rest?
[03:02] Carlos: Redwood Private supports your KMS — we can integrate with your AWS KMS using an IAM role; keys can be customer-managed and used for disk encryption and artifact storage. for HSM-level support we'd need to discuss a managed HSM integration; that's more bespoke.
[03:17] Maya: quick question on fallback: suppose eu-west-1 capacity is constrained, what does the failover look like? do we route to us-west-2? and will that break data residency requirements?
[03:27] Carlos: good point — our policy engine allows per-route rules: for EU-only workloads we can enforce strict locality, or we can configure a policy that attempts eu-west-1 and only fails to a compatible EU replica; if none available then block. we won't silently route EU personal data to US unless you opt in.
[03:43] Priya: perfect. timeline-wise, we want to pilot in us-west-2 first, then enable eu-west-1 by end of Q4. what's the usual provisioning lead time for a Private deployment in a new region?
[03:55] Carlos: standard is 2-4 weeks for initial infra and connectivity, plus time for your security review. for EU region it tends to be on the longer side due to audit/permitting — maybe 3-5 weeks.
[04:07] Ethan: about CIDR overlap — our VPC ranges are fairly large and some older accounts have overlapping ranges. do you support NATing or using TGW with translation?
[04:15] Carlos: we typically ask for non-overlapping ranges for peering; TGW helps with more advanced routing and you can use route tables to avoid overlap. if overlap is unavoidable we can use an egress proxy pattern or introduce a small NAT/translation VPC, but that's additional ops work. we'll include recommendations in the runbook.
[04:33] Samir (CTO): joined — hi all, quick note from exec: ROI is important, what's the cost delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private? also, do we retain the same API surface?
[04:43] Maya: yes, the API is the same. costs: hosted is usually lowest time-to-value but has per-token pricing; Dedicated reserved capacity reduces unit cost but requires a commit; Private is higher due to dedicated infra and networking but gives isolation and compliance. we can send you a pricing comparison matrix.
[05:02] Lena: are audit logs available as a push to our S3 or a logging endpoint?
[05:07] Carlos: yes, we can forward audit logs to your Kinesis/CloudWatch/S3 or provide syslog/SIEM forwarding. logs include request metadata, model/version, and token counts. PII is not logged by default unless explicitly configured.
[05:21] Priya: curious about egress — our compliance team wants all outbound traffic to be via our proxy. can Redwood route egress to customer-managed NAT?
[05:30] Carlos: you can push traffic to your egress VPC. two patterns: 1) Redwood VPC attaches to your TGW and your TGW egresses through your NAT; or 2) we use PrivateLink and your internal services call the endpoint which then routes through your proxy. both workable.
[05:46] Maya: any blockers on authentication? we support SAML-based SSO for the console and you can integrate with your IdP; for service-to-service auth we recommend mTLS or signed JWTs; we provide an identity provider pending examples in the docs.
[06:03] Lena: encryption in transit must be TLS 1.2+ and we want mutual TLS for service connections if possible.
[06:09] Carlos: mTLS is supported in our Private offering for control plane components; data plane TLS is always enforced. we'll note the mTLS cert rotation process.
[06:20] Priya: one more — what about software updates / maintenance windows? we need maintenance to be coordinated to avoid SLA impacts during our peak hours (night for EU).
[06:29] Carlos: maintenance is coordinated per-customer for Private deployments. we propose maintenance windows and have rollback policies. our SLA covers uptime for Dedicated/Private with credits for breaches.
[06:40] Maya: sounds good — I'll capture the key asks. quick recap from Redwood side: we'll send the VPC peering/TGW checklist, a sample Terraform/CF template, SOC2/ISO docs, and a pricing matrix. SE will run an initial latency test harness and propose the region topology.
[06:57] Priya: action items for us: share VPC CIDRs, transit gateway ARN, security contact, and any compliance checklist items.
[07:05] Samir: want us to run a small proof-of-concept to validate latency and residency?
[07:10] Maya: yes, small PoC makes sense — we can do a limited pilot in us-west-2, 2-4 nodes, low traffic. after pilot we evaluate EU rollout.
[07:18] Ethan: what's the limit for concurrent requests per node? we need to size for bursty telecom traffic.
[07:24] Carlos: depends on model and inference profile — we gave sample throughput numbers in the deck, but SE will size based on your prompt distribution. we'll ask for sample traffic profile.
[07:35] Priya: ok, we'll send sample traffic and token distribution.
[07:40] Maya: great. any final questions?
[07:44] Lena: none from security, thanks.
[07:46] Samir: all good. thanks team.
[07:50] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll circulate notes and next steps.

Meeting End.

Notes: transcription contains small mis-hears (e.g., "penging" was me trying to say "pending"). some technical terms may be slightly off but action items captured above.
